newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh ends first phase of tribal repatriation.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh ends first phase of tribal repatriation.

text.p: Bangladesh on Monday welcomed home the first of thousands of tribespeople who had spent more than 10 years in self-exile in India and said the door remained open for others to return soon.
A total of 6,717 refugees have returned in the first phase of repatration of up to 50,000 tribal refugees who fled to Tripura state to escape an insurrection by Shanti Bahini rebels, officials said.
The refugees began returning on March 28.

"We are delighted to have been able to complete the first round successfully. We will keep the doors open for those still huddling in Indian refugee camps to return in near future," said one official in Khagrachhari, one of three districts in Chittagong Hill Tracts and home to most of the 50,000 refugees.

The influx into India's Tripura state was triggered by battles between tribal Shanti Bahini guerrillas demanding political autonomy for the 5,500 sq-mile (14,200 sq-km) Hill Tracts bordering India and Burma.
Officials said the next phase was due to begin in a month.
Most of the returnees were taken from reception centres to their villages and resettled in homes which had been occupied by Bengalis for the past few years.
"We are trying to rehabilitate them (refugees) in their own homes...although it's a difficult task to drive away the settlers," one official told Reuters.
He said in some cases where settlers could not be removed the government had given them land to build new homes.
The returnees received money, construction materials and food under a deal between the government and tribal leaders.

"I received 15,000 taka ($344), two bundles of corrugated iron sheets for roofing, food for a month", said Maung Sui Thwai, who returned home this week. He said the authorities had pledged to provide rations for another eight months.
Mohammed Ismail, the Deputy Commissioner (administrator) of Khagrachhari, said: "We are doing everything to satisfy the returnees. They have nothing to fear."
"This time government seems to be keeping its pledges," said refugee leader Upendra Lal Chakma, supervising the repatriation.
He said more than 43,000 Bangladeshi tribespeople were still waiting to return home.
Officials say the Shanti Bahini insurgency, which started in 1973, has so far resulted in the deaths of more than 8,500 civilians, soldiers and rebels.
